title: Epizootic Ulcerative Syndrome (EUS) Technical Disease Card
authors: World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH / OIE)
publication: Aquatic Animal Health Code & Manual of Diagnostic Tests for Aquatic Animals
key_findings: Epizootic Ulcerative Syndrome is caused by the oomycete Aphanomyces invadans. It is characterized by severe necrotising ulcerative dermatitis followed by granulomatous myositis. Outbreaks frequently occur following sudden seasonal water temperature drops (below 25°C) and post-monsoon pH drops. Primary treatment revolves around water quality stabilization, application of agricultural lime (CaCO3) to buffer pH, and potassium permanganate or approved biocides in early stages.

title: Bacterial Diseases of Freshwater Carps in South Asia: Aeromonas and Flavobacterium complexes
key_findings: Bacterial fin and tail rot are predominantly opportunistic infections triggered by elevated organic load, un-ionized ammonia spikes (>0.03 mg/L), and sub-optimal dissolved oxygen (<4.0 mg/L). Lesions typically progress from distal fin margins proximally. Management includes 20-30% water exchange, reduction of feeding rate by 50% until mortality halts, and localized salt baths (2-3% NaCl dip) for breeding stock.

title: Streptococcosis in Warmwater Aquaculture: Tilapia Health Management Guide
publication: FAO Fisheries and Aquaculture Technical Paper 680
key_findings: Streptococcosis in Oreochromis niloticus causes acute septicemia and meningoencephalitis with classical signs of exophthalmia (pop-eye), corneal opacity, and erratic 'C-shape' spinning. Peak incidence coincides with high water temperatures (>31°C) combined with dissolved oxygen depression (<3.5 mg/L) and high stocking densities. Vaccination, density reduction, and emergency supplemental aeration are key preventive strategies.

title: Enteric Septicemia and Bacillary Necrosis in Pangasius hypophthalmus
authors: Network of Aquaculture Centres in Asia-Pacific (NACA)
key_findings: Edwardsiella ictaluri causes enteric septicemia in catfish, leading to petechial hemorrhages, severe ascites, and punctate lesions on the cranium. Poor sediment condition and accumulated un-ionized ammonia are major predisposing triggers. Feeding withholding during initial infection onset significantly lowers gut bacterial translocation.
